canonical_name: emcee 3.1.6 -- the MCMC Hammer: affine-invariant ensemble sampler (Foreman-Mackey, Hogg, Lang, Goodman)
lineage: Markov chain Monte Carlo (Metropolis et al. 1953; Hastings 1970) via Goodman & Weare's affine-invariant ensemble 'stretch move' (2010), implemented for astronomy (2012) and used in thousands of papers. A compact, inspectable sampler: walkers, proposals, acceptance fractions, autocorrelation time.
entry_points: emcee.EnsembleSampler(nwalkers, ndim, log_prob).run_mcmc(); get_chain(); get_autocorr_time(); acceptance_fraction

example.command: python harness: sample a 5-d correlated Gaussian, compare sample covariance to the truth
example.output: sample mean/covariance within tolerance of the analytic ORACLE; acceptance fraction in (0.2, 0.5)

upstream_docs: Foreman-Mackey, Hogg, Lang, Goodman, emcee: The MCMC Hammer, PASP 2013
Goodman & Weare, Ensemble samplers with affine invariance, CAMCoS 2010

human_capability_summary.built_to: draw samples from a posterior known only up to a constant, using an ensemble of walkers that adapts to the posterior's scale and orientation
human_capability_summary.pressure: high-dimensional, correlated, expensive likelihoods; hand-tuned proposal scales that fail when the posterior is anisotropic
human_capability_summary.success_means: sample moments match the target; autocorrelation time short relative to chain length

human_environmental_pressure: hidden parameters, expensive/black-box likelihood, anisotropic scales
human_failure_condition: the chain never mixes: acceptance ~0 or ~1, autocorrelation time longer than the run, moments wrong
behavioral_entry_point: shrink nwalkers to 2*ndim or stretch the target's condition number; watch acceptance and autocorrelation time

nyx_handoff.how_to_run_it: recipe.json (runner docker); python -m techne.fossils.harvest run emcee-3.1.6
nyx_handoff.what_humans_used_it_for: draw samples from a posterior known only up to a constant, using an ensemble of walkers that adapts to the posterior's scale and orientation
